sections.skill: Make pages readable on phones and forms accessible

questions.prompt: What is alt text?

choices.text: A short text description of an image
A second, alternative website for older visitors
A secret password typed to edit the website
The large heading at the top of each page

questions.correct_answer: A short text description of an image
questions.intro: Many visitors use phones, so check every page on a small screen. Text should be large enough to read without zooming, buttons big enough to tap, and nothing should require sideways scrolling. ACCESSIBILITY means people with disabilities can use the site too: give images short text descriptions (alt text), keep strong contrast between text and background, label every form field, and make forms short. A form with 3 fields is usually finished more often than one with 12.

sections.skill: Reading a menu in a dark restaurant

questions.prompt: Tiny gray letters in the dark are like what?

choices.text: Low-contrast small text on a phone
A clear, readable website on a phone

questions.correct_answer: Low-contrast small text on a phone
questions.intro: Imagine a menu with tiny gray letters in a dark restaurant: hard to read. Now imagine a menu with large dark letters on white paper and pictures described in words: easy for everyone, including someone with poor eyesight. A website on a phone is like that menu. Big clear text, labeled choices and descriptions of pictures help everyone order.
